material_class.structural_family: discrete dodecanuclear Cu6Gd6 cluster of six phenoxo-bridged Cu–Gd pairs linked by syn-anti carboxylates

synthesis.procedure: Hydroxylamine hydrochloride (0.0209 g, 0.3 mmol) and triethylamine (0.0304 g, 0.3 mmol) were added to methanol (3 mL) and dimethylformamide (6 mL) and stirred for about 15 min. A solution of 3-formylsalicylic acid (0.0498 g, 0.3 mmol) and triethylamine (0.0304 g, 0.3 mmol) in methanol/dimethylformamide (6 mL) was added. After 1 h, Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.0343 g, 0.1 mmol) was added and the solution was stirred for another hour. Cu(ClO4)2·6H2O (0.0371 g, 0.1 mmol) was then added. Green crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction formed directly from the reaction mixture by slow evaporation of the solvents at room temperature.

reagents.name: triethylamine
reagents.amount: 0.0304 g, 0.3 mmol, then a second portion of 0.0304 g, 0.3 mmol

synthesis.temperature: room temperature for crystallization; reaction temperature not stated
synthesis.time: about 15 min, then 1 h, then another 1 h before copper addition
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution mixing followed by slow solvent evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Green crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction were obtained directly from the reaction mixture by slow evaporation of the solvents at room temperature.

properties.summary: Phenoxo-bridged CuII–GdIII exchange is weakly ferromagnetic (J = +1.01 cm−1), giving an S = 4 ground state for each {CuGd} pair and a high-spin, weakly anisotropic Cu6Gd6 cluster. The magnetocaloric effect reaches ΔSm[0–7 T] = 23.5 J kg−1 K−1 (13.8 R) near 2.3 K.

measurements.name: χMT
measurements.conditions: 300 K; expected 49.5 cm3 mol−1 K for six CuII and six GdIII with g = 2

measurements.name: exchange coupling J(Cu–Gd)
measurements.conditions: fit of χMT(T) and M(B) to six independent {CuGd} pairs; gCu = gGd = 2.00; Hamiltonian H = −J SCu·SGd

measurements.name: Cu–Gd excited-state gap ΔE
measurements.conditions: ΔE = 4J between S = 4 ground multiplet and S = 3 excited multiplet

measurements.name: Gd axial anisotropy DGd
measurements.conditions: axial term used to simulate specific heat

measurements.name: upper limit of J(Gd–Gd)
measurements.conditions: phenomenological Schottky term fitted to low-temperature zero-field specific heat

measurements.name: magnetic entropy change ΔSm
measurements.conditions: ΔB = 0–7 T; peak near 2.3 K; equivalent to 13.8 R; entropy saturation above 10 K is 6R ln(16)
